correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite incidence theorem. The checker parses all 92 published tetrahedra, derives the 66-tetrahedron ball by the published star deletion, verifies face vector (15,93,145,66), reproduces exactly the 26 published boundary triangles, identifies 54 interior edges, exhaustively counts each edge degree, and verifies the histogram 1,14,21,13,5 at degrees 3,4,5,6,7. The distinguished edge is the sole degree-three edge and its three incident tetrahedra give link cycle 4-13-15. The lower bound degree at least 3 follows because an interior edge link in a triangulated 3-manifold is a simplicial circle.

value.rationale: The distinguished spanning edge is not arbitrary: it is the exact double-trefoil spanning edge used by Benedetti--Lutz to certify the canonical small non-collapsible ball. Its tetrahedron-incidence degree is the natural local complexity of that obstruction. Showing that this globally complicated knot sits on the unique interior edge of the smallest possible local degree separates knot complexity from local incidence complexity and gives a complete, motivated local spectrum rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
